newsitem.title: UK: LME copper eases on profit-taking, nickel weak.
newsitem.headline: LME copper eases on profit-taking, nickel weak.

text.p: LME copper retreated from highs in end-of-week profit taking as volume ebbed away ahead of the holidays.
Three-month prices peaked at $2,175, but eased back when they failed to breach this resistance point, ending slightly weaker at the kerb close at $2,150, down $5.
But the market still looked tight, with the premium of cash over three months metal firming about $4 to $107.
"The first half of January is tighter than January for a week or two weeks, which is due to buying and lending operations against averaging deals," a trader said.
Volume has been thin, but next week is expected to be even slower as the Christmas holidays on Wednesday and Thursday split the week in two.
Although chartists say copper technicals look buoyant, the lack of interest may curb the near-term upside scope for copper.
After $2,175, resistance is pegged at $2,215, then $2,300.
Nickel slipped, giving up all of Thursday's gains and creating a bearish outside day on the charts.
Prices shed $135 to $6,640 and could now be gearing up to test Monday's lows of $6,510.
Some analysts have set a target of $6,400.
Aluminium tried higher levels but pulled back from its high of $1,566, failing to confront resistance of $1,570.
Prices ended the day $5.50 firmer at $1,551.50.
Option dealers say there has been interest over the last few days in February and March $1,550 and $1,600 calls.
Tin finished weaker under the $5,800 level at $5,770, down $80 while lead ended the day unchanged at $714.
Zinc gained $3.50 to $1,065.50 and alloy ended $5 higher at $1,390/95.
